trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information (a name with a Social Security number, or a user name or email with a password, among other elements). The statute's covered entity includes a sole proprietorship (501.171(1)(b))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected individual in Florida, by mail or email; the notice gives the date or date range, the information involved, and a farm contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the 2 individuals whose W-9 data the farm holds; booking customers only if their passwords were exposed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals, never to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with a synopsis, the number affected, any services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Only if booking platform customer credentials (about 1,800 accounts) are part of the breach

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if booking platform customer credentials are part of the breach

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the farm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides; the farm will not rely on it when Social Security numbers were taken with names (farm policy)

obligation: Law enforcement delay of individual notice
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request
notify: Hold notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the farm (inbound)
trigger: A breach of a system kept by a third-party agent (booking platform vendor; accounting SaaS vendor)
deadline: Agent must notify the farm no later than 10 days after its determination and give the farm the information it needs; the farm then gives the notices above
notify: The farm (owner-operator; farm security contact registered with each vendor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track with the booking and accounting vendors

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected customers or individuals who live outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of every affected person (nearly all customers live in Florida)

obligation: Produce Safety records on FDA request during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: FDA asks for qualified exemption records while SYS-09, SYS-10, or the laptop is unavailable
deadline: Readily available; 24 hours for records kept offsite; electronic records in an accessible and legible format
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - a qualified exempt farm is subject to Subpart O (112.6(a)(2)); the monthly exports (POL-01 8.4) are the fallback

trigger: Determination that an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the duty is on a responsible party, the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)(1)); the farm registers none. If fertigation tampering could have affected fruit, close the affected U-pick block and stop sales from it until checked

obligation: FAA small UAS safety event report
trigger: A drone operation causes serious injury, loss of consciousness, or property damage over $500 (other than the drone)
deadline: No later than 10 calendar days after the operation
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a drone operation is involved (for example a compromised ground-station tablet leads to a crash); remote pilot in command reports

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
deadline: As soon as practical (Day 1 in the runbook)
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; supports investigation and OFAC mitigation

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, food and agriculture entities are covered only above the SBA size standard, and the farm is far below it

trigger: Suspected compromise of the phone or card reader app
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the phone or card reader is involved; card data does not enter farm systems
No cyber policy; call the insurer on Day 1 to ask whether any cyber coverage applies before hiring outside help

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the farm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (the NRCS contract is a cost-share agreement)

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services)
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the farm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
